summary: Sustained p95/p99 latency uplift on dedicated pool during autoscaler smoothing window causing client timeouts
description: Issue summary: TellusAI reported a sustained increase in tail latency (p95/p99) for requests routed to their dedicated GPU pool during the regional autoscaler smoothing period. Impact: Several of their production routes experienced 504/timeout errors and elevated token latency for ~45 minutes. Environment: Dedicated pool (TellusAI-reserved-1), us-west-2, production traffic between 2026-03-13T15:02 and 2026-03-13T15:50 UTC. Observed behavior: p50 unchanged, p95 rose from ~230ms to ~1.7s, p99 spiked to 3.6s. Throughput (requests/sec) for the pool decreased 18% during the window while queued request depth increased 2.3x. This ticket captures Support/SRE investigation and mitigation steps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route production traffic through dedicated pool TellusAI-reserved-1 in us-west-2
2) Simulate a short simultaneous tenant burst (30s) from multiple small sessions to emulate tenant grooming behavior
3) Observe autoscaler smoothing and lock (configured smoothing_window=60s) kick in while worker attachments/evictions happen
4) Measure p95/p99 latency and request queue depth in the serving runtime and scheduler during the smoothing window

investigation_notes: Initial triage: metrics show autoscaler entered smoothing due to rapid short-lived connection spikes from other tenants in same pool. While smoothing, new workers were not attached quickly enough and prefetch/batch assembly latencies grew.
Hypothesis A: Noisy neighbors producing many short streams caused frequent small-batch arrivals that fragmented batcher efficiency and kept GPU streaming contexts busy with high overhead per stream.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler smoothing configuration prevented timely scale-up during a compound small-stream fanout, causing transient slot scarcity and increased KV-prefetch backpressure.
Telemetry examined: scheduler attach latencies, worker-attach-fail counts, autoscaler decision logs, batch_assembly_delay distribution, KV cache hit ratio, and GPU occupancy trends.

Findings: batch_assembly_delay correlated with moments when ephemeral tenants peaked. Worker attach latencies spiked to 1.2s for new GPUs during the window. KV cache miss rate increased by 14% for TellusAI's model variant during peak.

Cross-references: similar pattern to SUP-331122 (ephemeral attach fanout causing degradation) but here the smoothing parameter amplified impact because scale-up decisions were delayed intentionally to avoid oscillation.
Temporary mitigation applied: routed TellusAI traffic to a higher-priority shard (canary fallback) and increased reserved burst capacity for 30 minutes to drain queue. This reduced p99 to ~420ms.

Longer-term items: consider autoscaler policy tweak (smaller smoothing window for dedicated pools with high small-stream variance), and implement per-tenant short-stream detection to bias scale-up decisions.

resolution: Workaround: During incident we rerouted TellusAI traffic to a dedicated fallback shard and temporarily increased burst reservation; this restored p95/p99 to acceptable levels. Fix applied: autoscaler smoothing_window reduced from 60s to 20s for pool TellusAI-reserved-1 and short-stream detection flag enabled to prioritize scale-up when small-stream fanout is detected. Rollout: change deployed to staging on 2026-03-14 and promoted to us-west-2 dedicated pools 2026-03-14T11:00 UTC with gradual canary. Follow-ups: engineering to add a metric for short-stream fanout ratio and create an alert if short_stream_ratio > 0.35 for >2min. Owner: Arjun Patel (SRE) for config and telemetry, Product for policy review.
